assumptions: Header layout: second-block W0 (merkle tail), W1 (time), W3 (nonce) vary; W2 (bits) and padding are fixed. The first block's midstate is random per header.
A hit means the hash, read as Bitcoin's little-endian 256-bit number, has k leading zero bits, i.e. it is <= 2^(256-k) - 1: the real target comparison for a target of that form.
Reduced-round variants cut all three compressions to r rounds; conditions are taken from the r-round computation itself.
Expected work counts SHA256d evaluations; a condition check costs 5/128 of one (5 of 128 compression rounds) and is charged.

Neighbour strategy cost treats each neighbour as a fresh candidate (a real implementation scans only nonces whose flipped bits are 0, so neighbours fall outside the scan); the measured conditional rate is what decides it.
Significance: two-sided z against the null rate, Bonferroni over all round counts and tests.
baseline: Exhaustive search over fresh nonces: 2^k_target SHA256d evaluations per target hit (measured on the same scan).
conclusion: REDUCED-ROUND ONLY: deviations were detected only for reduced-round variants. These say nothing about full 64-round SHA-256/SHA-256d and give no mining advantage; full-round configurations (where tested) showed no deviation. Trail search over 592 controllable differences: best survives to round 5 of the second header block within 24 bits. Full SHA256d: neighbours of share hits hit the 2^-12 target at 1.0040x the null rate (z +0.36); the neighbour strategy needs 0.9997x the exhaustive work per hit. Inputs satisfying the 11 trail conditions hit 4-bit / 8-bit / 12-bit levels at 1.010x / 0.966x / 1.032x the null rate. Round counts where some strategy beats the null rate: [4, 5].

dataset.description: Header h: 80 random bytes from SplitMix64::stream(seed, h); nonces i * 0x9e3779b1 for i = 0, 1, ... (a bijection on 32 bits), at most 16x the expected scan per header.

errata.note: Assumption error found 2026-11-22: W0 (merkle-root bytes 32..35) cannot differ under one midstate, because the root's other 28 bytes are in header block 1; a W0 difference with an unchanged midstate needs a 224-bit merkle-root collision. The W0 trail candidates and the W0 part of the neighbour set are therefore unreachable for a miner. The W1 (time) and W3 (nonce) results stand, and so does the conclusion (no mining advantage). trail-sat-0001 excludes W0.

hypothesis: A validated reduced-round characteristic, or neighbour relations along trail differences in the header words a miner controls, raises the conditional probability of the Bitcoin target event enough to lower the expected work per target hit below exhaustive search.
methodology: A: trail search with the signed estimator, top trails measured on header-structured pairs. B: per round count, scan nonces of random headers until `share_hits` share-level hits; evaluate every neighbour x ^ Δ for Δ in the 32 nonce bits plus the top trail differences; count target-level hits. C: during the same scan, evaluate the 11 conditions of the nonce-MSB trail on each nonce and split target hits by whether they hold. Strategy costs from these counts.
name: Trail-to-search conversion for SHA256d(header) <= target
null_hypothesis: For every tested difference and condition set, the target-hit probability of neighbours of share hits and of condition-satisfying inputs equals 2^-k_target, so every derived strategy needs at least the exhaustive work per hit.

reproduction.method: full rerun with identical seed and parameters on a separate Rayon pool with a different thread count; SHA-256 of the canonical deterministic results compared

verification.detail: 512 share hits and their neighbours identical
verification.method: independent SHA-256 over the full serialized header recomputes scanned hashes and the W3-bit-0 neighbour of each share hit (first header, 64 share hits per round count)
